lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Care and Basic Food Safety
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: kitchen reset

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice kitchen reset. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Before learning the kitchen-specific safe routine, the learner notices what "reset" would even mean in three kitchen zones — counters, sink, and table — and attempts a first pass at resetting all three on their own, leaving the stove and any knives or sharp tools for an adult to handle.
safetyNotes: The stove, oven, and any knives or sharp tools are adult-only for this lesson; the learner does not touch them.
Stop and ask for help with anything unfamiliar, broken glass, or a spill that smells unusual.

simulationAlternative.description: If the household kitchen isn't available to reset (shared or restricted space), the learner instead describes, zone by zone, what a full counters/sink/table reset would involve for a kitchen shown in a printed or hand-drawn scene, naming the same stove-and-knife boundary.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: What is different about resetting a kitchen compared to resetting a space like your bedroom or the living room? Name one specific kitchen-only consideration.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Zone completion: All three zones visibly reset. | Boundary awareness: Learner stays within the boundary without being reminded. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Add a fourth kitchen zone (like the refrigerator door or a pantry shelf) to the reset routine and compare, in writing, how resetting that zone was different from the first three.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice kitchen reset. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: kitchen reset worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before learning the kitchen-specific safe routine, the learner notices what "reset" would even mean in three kitchen zones — counters, sink, and table — and attempts a first pass at resetting all three on their own, leaving the stove and any knives or sharp tools for an adult to handle.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact kitchen reset decision or action.
Model move 2: Before resetting, look at the kitchen and predict which of the three zones (counters, sink, table) will take the most work, and why.
Model move 3: Reset the three zones: clear and wipe the counters, load or clear the sink, and clear and wipe the table.
Model check: Zone completion: All three zones visibly reset. | Boundary awareness: Learner stays within the boundary without being reminded.

resources.title: kitchen reset action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for kitchen reset.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: kitchen reset coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before learning the kitchen-specific safe routine, the learner notices what "reset" would even mean in three kitchen zones — counters, sink, and table — and attempts a first pass at resetting all three on their own, leaving the stove and any knives or sharp tools for an adult to handle.
Coach direction: Before resetting, look at the kitchen and predict which of the three zones (counters, sink, table) will take the most work, and why.
Learner prompt: State your prediction and reasoning.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: kitchen reset complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Reset the three zones: clear and wipe the counters, load or clear the sink, and clear and wipe the table. Do not touch the stove, oven, or any knives — leave those for your adult.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I reset all three zones without touching the stove, oven, or sharp tools.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Which zone took the longest, and did that match your prediction?

Equal-access rule: If the household kitchen isn't available to reset (shared or restricted space), the learner instead describes, zone by zone, what a full counters/sink/table reset would involve for a kitchen shown in a printed or hand-drawn scene, naming the same stove-and-knife boundary.

resources.title: kitchen reset minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is different about resetting a kitchen compared to resetting a space like your bedroom or the living room? Name one specific kitchen-only consideration.
Success checks: Zone completion: All three zones visibly reset. | Boundary awareness: Learner stays within the boundary without being reminded.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: kitchen reset supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional kitchen reset condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.
Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Zone completion: All three zones visibly reset. | Boundary awareness: Learner stays within the boundary without being reminded..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u03-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: kitchen reset — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Reset the three zones: clear and wipe the counters, load or clear the sink, and clear and wipe the table. Do not touch the stove, oven, or any knives — leave those for your adult.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
